01 / The Origin · A meme from two languages · 壹 · 起源

The Meme Story

From a simple question to a legendary meme. Two unlikely friends swept a temple courtyard — and a tiny warrior with a sword and shield was born.

It started with a question

In 2014, a short Vine skit turned a dog reaching for mints into the unforgettable line: “What the dog doing?” The internet did what it does — reposts, reaction videos and remixed audio carried the catchphrase everywhere.

Years later, Chinese listeners heard the phrase differently. “What the dog doing?” sounded like 我的刀盾 (wǒ de dāo dùn) — “my sword and shield.” So the internet did the only logical thing: it gave the dog a sword and a shield.

The result is Drog: a Cheems Shiba face on a round frog body, armed for a battle nobody declared, guarding a courtyard nobody asked him to guard. Know Your Meme recorded the character in March 2026.

Now the dog crosses chains. This page is his Canton Network chapter — same dog, same confusion, new home — and now with his own token: $DROG, live on SupaNova. The specs are in the next section.

Meet the most confused warrior

Nobody knows.
Not even the dog.

He has a sword. He has a shield. He has marched all the way to Canton Network. Ask him what he’s doing there and he will simply smile, the way he always does.

05 / The Accidental Translation

Lost in translation. Found in memes.

It’s not a literal translation. It’s an internet mishearing — a sound-alike joke called 空耳 (soramimi). That’s why the dog got equipped for battle.

07 / Good Questions, Bad Dog

Dog Questions.

Everything you wanted to know but were too confused to ask.

What does “我的刀盾” mean?+

Literally, it means “my sword and shield.” As a meme, it’s a playful Chinese sound-alike of “What the dog doing?” — not a real translation.

Where did “What the Dog Doing?” come from?+

The English catchphrase traces back to a 2014 Vine skit associated with Tony Baker, where a dog unexpectedly joins people reaching for mints. It spread widely through reposts and reaction edits.

Who is the sword-and-shield dog?+

The community-recognized 我的刀盾 — Drog — is a wonderfully absurd Shiba-faced, frog-bodied character holding a blade and a shield. He gives the Chinese pun a visual identity. The drawing on this page is this site’s own Drog.

Is there a token on Canton?+

Yes — $DROG is live on Canton Network. Canton tokens don’t use an EVM-style contract address; the token is identified by its token page ID (5a784c56-68b6-500b-ab14-18e9c85ebd90). Full specs are in the Token Specs section above — if a different “DROG” link is circulating, it is not this dog.

Where and how do I buy it?+

$DROG is live on SupaNova — buy it on the official SupaNova page: connect your Canton wallet, enter the amount, and confirm. $DROG is on the bonding curve (stage “New”, 250K CC to graduation).

Why Canton Network?+

Because every legendary meme eventually wanders somewhere new. Canton is the public, privacy-enabled blockchain built for institutional finance — serious infrastructure, meet the least serious dog on the internet. He brought his own security: one sword, one shield.

Is this financial advice?+

No. This is a meme-driven fan page, not a promise of profit or utility, and nothing here is financial advice. The dog himself holds no assets — his paws are full.

How can I take part?+

Make a PFP in the Dog Lab above, share your own edits and captions, and spread the question wherever dogs are doing things. Credit original creators when reusing their work.
